blocks.text: In 1910 Thomas Hunt Morgan found a male Drosophila with white eyes instead of the normal red. He crossed this mutant male with a normal (wild-type) red-eyed female, and all the F1 flies had red eyes, so red was dominant to white.

He then crossed red-eyed F1 flies with each other. In the F2 there were 3473 red-eyed flies (males and females) and 782 white-eyed flies, about 18%. The ratio of red to white was greater than 3:1, but the striking point was that all the white-eyed F2 flies were males.

blocks.alt: Three rows with a fly and its pair of sex chromosomes in a circle. Parents: a white-eyed male XrY (a white X with the recessive allele r and a hooked Y with no allele) x a red-eyed female XRXR (two dark red X chromosomes with the dominant allele R). F1: a red-eyed male XRY x a red-eyed female XRXr. F2: a white-eyed male XrY, a red-eyed male XRY, a red-eyed female XRXr and a red-eyed female XRXR.
blocks.caption: Figure 18.14: Inheritance of sex-linked trait (eye colour) in Drosophila (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 18.14).
blocks.long_description: Labels: X-chromosome with recessive white-eye allele (r), Y-chromosome with no allele, X-chromosomes with dominant red-eye allele (R), Parents, F1 generation, F2 generation.

blocks.text: To test whether a white-eyed female could exist, Morgan testcrossed an F1 red-eyed female with a white-eyed male and obtained white-eyed and red-eyed males and females in a 1:1:1:1 ratio, so females could have white eyes. He then mated a white-eyed female with a red-eyed male: all the daughters had red eyes and all the sons white eyes.

blocks.title: Morgan's conclusion
blocks.text: The white-eye gene is on the X chromosome, and the Y chromosome does not carry an allele of it. Morgan called such genes sex-linked genes and the traits sex-linked traits.
Embryonic screening means methods that check embryos for genetic disorders and an abnormal number of chromosomes, such as ultrasound scanning, chorionic villus sampling and amniocentesis.

Amniocentesis is generally done between the 15th and 20th weeks of pregnancy. A long needle is inserted into the amniotic sac while an ultrasound probe locates the foetus; the needle draws out some amniotic fluid containing foetal cells, which are kept in a culture medium and checked for an abnormal number of chromosomes.

blocks.alt: A side section of a pregnant abdomen with the spine below. Inside the uterus the foetus lies in the amniotic sac filled with amniotic fluid. An ultrasound probe rests on the skin above, and the needle of a syringe passes through the abdominal wall into the amniotic sac. An arrow leads to an enlarged circle of foetal cells.
